answer: We formulate a protocol where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds are tied to zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions, requiring nodes to broadcast a cryptographically verified signal at the dawn of every epoch. If an adversary attempts identity multiplication across a high-latency canyon, a subgame-perfect slashing matrix scales capital requirements linearly while forcing expected attack utility strictly below zero. Consequently, maintaining a singular collateralized node converges to a unique, robust strict Nash equilibrium in adversarial environments.
